# GovStack Scheduler BB — Gap Analysis for CivicOS Appointments BB

**Spec source:** [GovStackWorkingGroup/bb-scheduler](https://github.com/GovStackWorkingGroup/bb-scheduler)
**OpenAPI spec:** `api/Govstack_scheduler_BB_APIs.json` (37 endpoints, 9 API groups)
**CivicOS target:** `apps/appointments/`
**Date:** 2026-07-24
**Author:** Auto-generated by gap analysis

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The CivicOS Appointments BB has a rich model layer (16 model classes, ~2 300 lines) and a
complete service layer for the core booking lifecycle. However, it has **zero HTTP endpoints**.
`apps/appointments/urls.py` is an empty stub with only placeholder comments.

The GovStack Scheduler BB specification requires **37 REST endpoints** across 9 API groups.
Of the 9 GovStack entity types, only 3 have any corresponding CivicOS model. Three are
completely absent from the data model; the remaining 3 exist only partially.

The work to reach certifiability is therefore primarily **HTTP / API surface work** backed by
new models for 3 entity types that don't yet exist.

---

## 2. GovStack Scheduler BB — Specification Overview

### 2.1 Four Actor Roles

| Actor | GovStack Term | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| System administrator | Admin | Manages entities, resources, affiliations |
| Service organizer | Organizer | Creates events, schedules alerts, manages messages |
| Bookable resource | Resource | Receives alerts; status-poll URL; availability queries |
| Citizen / beneficiary | Subscriber | Books appointments; receives reminders |

### 2.2 Required Capabilities per Actor

**Admin:**
- Register / manage entities (organizations)
- Register / manage resources and affiliations
- View logs

**Organizer:**
- Create / modify / cancel events (appointment slots)
- Schedule alerts for event participants
- Manage message templates
- Create appointments (bookings) for subscribers

**Resource:**
- Query own availability
- Receive alert notifications via callback URL

**Subscriber:**
- Register as subscriber
- Book an appointment (exclusive or shared)
- Reschedule or cancel their booking
- Receive confirmation and reminder messages

## 4. CivicOS Existing Implementation

### 4.1 Model Inventory (`apps/appointments/models.py` — 2 334 lines)

| Model | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Organization` | Gov department / NGO. Top-level tenant boundary. |
| `SchedulingPolicy` | Configurable booking rules (lead times, buffers, cancellation window). |
| `ServiceType` | Category of service (e.g. "Driver's Licence Renewal"). |
| `AppointmentType` | Specific offering within a ServiceType (duration, mode, consent gate, document gate). |
| `Location` | Physical or virtual office. Belongs to Organization. |
| `Resource` | Meeting room / video room / equipment. Belongs to Location. |
| `StaffProfile` | Staff member scheduling profile. Linked to `AUTH_USER_MODEL`. |
| `AvailabilityTemplate` | Weekly recurring schedule for a StaffProfile. |
| `StaffException` | One-off availability overrides (holidays, blocked times). |
| `Slot` | A concrete bookable time window generated from AvailabilityTemplate. |
| `Booking` | Client reservation against a Slot. State machine: pending → confirmed → cancelled / completed / rejected. UUID PK. |
| `Attendee` | Additional attendees on a Booking. |
| `BookingAuditLog` | Immutable append-only audit record for every Booking state change. |
| `WaitlistEntry` | Queue for oversubscribed AppointmentTypes (future wave). |
| `QueueEntry` | Walk-in virtual queue (future wave). |
| `ClientNoShowRecord` | Citizen no-show tracking with suspension logic. |

### 4.2 Service Layer (`apps/appointments/services/`)

| File | Functions |
|---|---|
| `booking.py` | `create_booking()`, `confirm_booking()`, `cancel_booking()`, `reschedule_booking()`, `mark_no_show()`, `complete_booking()`, `reject_booking()` |
| `availability.py` | Staff availability computation (reads AvailabilityTemplate + StaffException) |
| `slots.py` | Slot generation and management |

Custom exceptions: `BookingError`, `SlotFullError`, `CitizenSuspendedError`, `FrequencyWindowError`, `MaxActiveBookingsError`, `RescheduleCountError`, `RescheduleWindowError`, `InvalidStatusTransitionError`.

```python
    # Citizen views — Wave 5
    # Staff views — Wave 5
    # API endpoints — Wave 8
]
```

**Status: completely empty.**

## 5. Data Model Mapping — GovStack vs CivicOS

| GovStack Entity | CivicOS Model | Gap Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Entity** | `Organization` | ⚠️ Model exists — 0 API endpoints |
| **Resource** | `Resource` + `StaffProfile` | ⚠️ Partial — missing `alert_url`, `alert_preference`, `status_poll_url`, `category` string; no API |
| **Subscriber** | *(none)* | ❌ No model exists |
| **Affiliation** | *(none)* | ❌ No model exists |
| **Event** | `AppointmentType` + `Slot` | ⚠️ Partial — different structural model; no API |
| **Appointment** | `Booking` | ⚠️ Partial — missing `exclusive`, `participant_type`, `participant_entity_id`; no API |
| **AlertSchedule** | *(none)* | ❌ No model exists |
| **Message** | *(none)* | ❌ No model exists |
| **Log** | `BookingAuditLog` | ⚠️ Partial — not exposed as API resource; read-only in admin only |

### 5.1 Entity → Organization Mapping

| GovStack Field | CivicOS Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `category` | `organization_type` | CivicOS uses controlled vocab; GovStack is free string |
| `name` | `name_en` / `name_fr` | CivicOS is bilingual; GovStack is single `name` |
| `phone` | *(missing)* | Must be added to `Organization` model |
| `email` | *(missing)* | Must be added to `Organization` model |
| `website` | *(missing)* | Must be added to `Organization` model |
| entity_id (auto) | `pk` (int) | GovStack expects a string ID; expose as `str(pk)` |

### 5.2 Resource → Resource / StaffProfile Mapping

GovStack Resource covers both physical resources AND staff. CivicOS splits these into
`Resource` (rooms/equipment) and `StaffProfile` (people). The GovStack `category` field
determines which type of resource is meant.

| GovStack Field | CivicOS Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `name_en` | Bilingual in CivicOS |
| `category` | `resource_type` | CivicOS: `room`, `equipment`, `virtual`, `phone_line`, `other` |
| `phone` | *(missing on Resource)* | Present on `StaffProfile.user.phone_number`; must add to `Resource` |
| `email` | *(missing on Resource)* | Present on `StaffProfile.user.email`; must add to `Resource` |
| `alert_url` | *(missing)* | New field — callback URL for push alerts |
| `alert_preference` | *(missing)* | New field — `"push"` / `"poll"` / `"email"` etc. |
| `status_poll_url` | *(missing)* | New field — URL that GovStack polls for resource availability status |
| resource_id (auto) | `pk` (int) | Expose as `str(pk)` |

### 5.3 Subscriber → (Missing Model)

GovStack Subscriber = a citizen who can receive appointments.

CivicOS has no `Subscriber` model. Citizens are Django `AUTH_USER_MODEL` users, and the
`Booking.citizen` FK links them to appointments. The GovStack Subscriber adds fields that
CivicOS does not track on the citizen:

| GovStack Field | CivicOS equivalent | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `user.get_full_name()` | Derivable — no separate model needed |
| `category` | *(none)* | New concept — subscriber category (e.g. "individual", "group") |
| `phone` | `user.phone_number` | Derivable |
| `email` | `user.email` | Derivable |
| `alert_url` | *(none)* | New — push alert endpoint for this subscriber |
| `alert_preference` | *(none)* | New — notification channel preference |
| `status_poll_url` | *(none)* | New — URL GovStack polls for subscriber availability |

**Decision:** Create a `GovStackSubscriberProfile` model that extends the existing User model
with the new fields, or project User model fields onto the GovStack Subscriber schema at the
API layer (simpler but less faithful to spec).

### 5.4 Affiliation → (Missing Model)

GovStack Affiliation links a Resource to an Entity with a work schedule.

CivicOS has no Affiliation model. The nearest equivalent is `StaffProfile`, which links a
staff user to locations, but this is structurally different — CivicOS uses
`AvailabilityTemplate` for scheduling, not a simple `work_days_hours` object on an
affiliation record.

**Decision:** Create a `GovStackAffiliation` model:
```python
class GovStackAffiliation(TimestampedModel):
    resource = ForeignKey(Resource, ...)   # or StaffProfile
    entity = ForeignKey(Organization, ...) # which org this resource is affiliated with
    resource_category = CharField(...)
    work_days_hours = JSONField(...)       # GovStack days_hours structure
```

### 5.5 Event → AppointmentType + Slot Mapping

GovStack "Event" is a schedulable occurrence with slots. CivicOS splits this into:
- `AppointmentType` (the configuration / template)
- `Slot` (a concrete bookable instance)

This is structurally richer than GovStack's Event but GovStack-compatible at the API surface
by projecting a `Slot` (plus its parent `AppointmentType` metadata) as a GovStack Event.

| GovStack Field | CivicOS Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `AppointmentType.name_en` | |
| `description` | `AppointmentType.description_en` | |
| `category` | `ServiceType.category` | |
| `host_entity_id` | `Location.organization_id` | |
| `slots` | `Slot` queryset | Array of slot start/end times |
| `deadline` | `Slot.start_datetime - SchedulingPolicy.min_lead_time_hours` | Computed |
| `subscriber_limit` | `Slot.capacity` | |
| `terms` | `AppointmentType.requires_consent` + consent text | |
| `status` | `Slot.status` | `available`, `partial`, `full`, `cancelled` |
| `venue` | `Location` address fields | Must denormalize Location into GovStack venue struct |
| `from` | `Slot.start_datetime` | |
| `to` | `Slot.end_datetime` | |

### 5.6 Appointment → Booking Mapping

| GovStack Field | CivicOS Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `exclusive` | *(implicit: Slot.capacity == 1)* | Must derive from Slot or add explicit flag |
| `event_id` | `Booking.slot_id` | |
| `participant_type` | `"subscriber"` (always) | GovStack distinguishes resource vs subscriber attendee |
| `participant_id` | `Booking.citizen_id` | |
| `status_id` | `Booking.status` | |
| `participant_entity_id` | `Booking.slot.location.organization_id` | Derivable |

### 5.7 AlertSchedule → (Missing Model)

GovStack AlertSchedule = a scheduled push notification to all participants of an event.

CivicOS sends reminders via Celery tasks (`reminder_72h`, `reminder_24h`, `reminder_2h`)
stored as task IDs on the `Booking` model. These are per-booking, not per-event.

GovStack AlertSchedule is event-scoped (targets all participants of an event), supports a
`target_category` filter, and references a `Message` template.

**Decision:** Create a `GovStackAlertSchedule` model:
```python
class GovStackAlertSchedule(TimestampedModel):
    event = ForeignKey(Slot, ...)              # the event (slot) to alert for
    target_category = CharField(...)           # which participants to notify
    message = ForeignKey(GovStackMessage, ...) # message template to use
    alert_datetime = DateTimeField(...)        # when to send the alert
    celery_task_id = CharField(...)            # revokeable Celery ETA task
```

### 5.8 Message → (Missing Model)

GovStack Message = a reusable notification template (owned by an Entity).

CivicOS has email notification templates as Django template files in
`templates/notifications/email/`. There is no database-backed message template model.

**Decision:** Create a `GovStackMessage` model:
```python
class GovStackMessage(TimestampedModel):
    entity = ForeignKey(Organization, ...)
    category = CharField(...)    # "reminder", "confirmation", "cancellation", etc.
    message_body = TextField()   # plain text or HTML body
```

### 5.9 Log → BookingAuditLog Mapping

CivicOS `BookingAuditLog` is append-only (immutable). GovStack Log supports full CRUD
(including DELETE and PUT), which conflicts with the audit invariant.

**Decision:** Expose `BookingAuditLog` read-only on the GovStack `/log/list_details` endpoint,
and implement `/log/new` as a gateway to `_write_audit_log()`. Reject PUT and DELETE on
audit log entries with `HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed` or a custom error code (preserving
immutability).

| GovStack Field | CivicOS Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `logger_role` | `BookingAuditLog.actor_role` | Must add `actor_role` field |
| `logger_id` | `BookingAuditLog.actor_id` | Present (`actor` FK) |
| `entity_id` | `Booking.slot.location.organization_id` | Derivable via join |
| `log_category` | `BookingAuditLog.action` | Present |
| `datetime` | `BookingAuditLog.created_at` | Present |
| `log_data` | `BookingAuditLog.event_detail` | Present (JSON) |

- `email = EmailField(blank=True)`
- `website = URLField(blank=True)`

**`Resource` model — add:**

- `email = EmailField(blank=True)`

### 6.4 Missing Serializers

All 37 endpoints need DRF serializers following the GovStack schema convention, where
request bodies use `qry` wrapper objects and responses use list containers:

```
event_new_qry → { details: event_creation_details }
event_get_details_qry → { event_filter: {...}, event_details_required: {...} }
```

CivicOS uses standard DRF serializers; these GovStack envelope wrappers must be
implemented for each of the 9 entity types.

### 6.5 GovStack Auth Convention

GovStack uses `requestor_id` + `request_token` as **query parameters** on every call:
```
GET /event/list_details?requestor_id=XXX&request_token=YYY&qry=...
```

CivicOS uses `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` header or Django session auth.

**Decision:** Implement `GovStackSchedulerAuth` authentication class that:
1. Validates `request_token` against the `GovStackRegisteredBB` registry (already present
   in `apps/payments/govstack_models.py` as `GovStackRegisteredBB`)
2. Resolves `requestor_id` to a Django user / actor identity
3. Falls through to standard JWT if `requestor_id` / `request_token` absent

## 7. Implementation Plan (Wave-by-Wave)

### Wave A — Foundation (Pre-requisites)

**Goal:** Create the missing models and wire the GovStack auth convention.

**Tasks:**
1. Add `phone`, `email`, `website` to `Organization` → migration
2. Add `phone`, `email`, `alert_url`, `alert_preference`, `status_poll_url` to `Resource` → migration
3. Add `actor_role` to `BookingAuditLog` → migration; backfill existing records
4. Create `GovStackMessage` model → migration
5. Create `GovStackAffiliation` model → migration
6. Create `GovStackAlertSchedule` model + Celery task skeleton → migration
7. Create `GovStackSubscriberProfile` model (optional OneToOne on User) → migration
8. Create `apps/appointments/govstack_auth.py` — `GovStackSchedulerAuth` class
9. Create `apps/appointments/govstack_serializers.py` — all 9 entity serializer sets
10. Wire `apps/appointments/govstack_urls.py` into `config/urls.py` at prefix `/gs/scheduler/`

**Migrations:** 1 per model group (or 1 combined migration `0013_govstack_fields`)
**Files to create:** `govstack_auth.py`, `govstack_serializers.py`, `govstack_urls.py`, `govstack_views.py`

---

### Wave B — Entity + Resource + Affiliation Endpoints (Admin APIs)

**Goal:** All 13 endpoints that admin actors need.

**Endpoints:**
- `POST/PUT/DELETE/GET /entity/...` (4 endpoints)
- `POST/PUT/DELETE/GET /resource/...` + `GET /resource/availability` (5 endpoints)
- `POST/PUT/DELETE/GET /affiliation/...` (4 endpoints)

**Service layer needed:**
- `apps/appointments/services/govstack_entity.py` — CRUD around `Organization`
- `apps/appointments/services/govstack_resource.py` — CRUD around `Resource` / `StaffProfile`
- `apps/appointments/services/govstack_affiliation.py` — CRUD around `GovStackAffiliation`

**Key complexity:** `/resource/availability` must query `Slot` availability filtered by
`entity_id` and date range — this bridges into the existing `slots.py` service.

---

### Wave C — Subscriber Endpoints

**Goal:** 4 subscriber endpoints (citizen registration in GovStack terms).

**Endpoints:**
- `POST/PUT/DELETE/GET /subscriber/...`

**Notes:**
- `POST /subscriber/new` maps to creating / updating a Django User + `GovStackSubscriberProfile`
- `DELETE /subscriber` should soft-delete (set `user.is_active = False`)
- Requires PIPEDA-careful design: citizen PII in request must not appear in logs

---

### Wave D — Event Endpoints

**Goal:** 4 event endpoints (slot / appointment-type management).

**Endpoints:**
- `POST/PUT/DELETE/GET /event/...`

**Key complexity:** GovStack Event combines CivicOS `AppointmentType` + `Slot` + `Location`
into a single flat object. The service layer must:
1. Deserialize a GovStack Event `creation_details` into the appropriate CivicOS objects
2. Accept a `slots` array (each with `from`/`to`) and generate `Slot` records
3. Serialize multiple CivicOS models back into a GovStack Event shape on GET

**Service layer needed:**
- `apps/appointments/services/govstack_event.py`

---

### Wave E — Appointment Endpoints

**Goal:** 4 appointment (booking) endpoints — the core citizen-facing booking flow.

**Endpoints:**
- `POST/PUT/DELETE/GET /appointment/...`

**Mapping:**
- `POST /appointment/new` → `services/booking.py:create_booking()`
- `PUT /appointment/modifications` → `services/booking.py:reschedule_booking()` or status update
- `DELETE /appointment` → `services/booking.py:cancel_booking()`
- `GET /appointment/list_details` → `Booking.objects.filter(...)` with GovStack filter schema

**Key complexity:** GovStack uses `participant_type` + `participant_id` where CivicOS uses
`Booking.citizen` FK. Must resolve `participant_id` (GovStack subscriber_id) → Django User PK.

### Wave F — Message + AlertSchedule Endpoints

**Status: implemented.** `apps/appointments/services/govstack_message.py`,
`services/govstack_alert_schedule.py`, 8 views in `govstack_views.py`, the
`dispatch_alert_schedule` Celery task (`apps/appointments/tasks.py`) with a
fail-closed SSRF-safe outbound URL validator (HTTPS-only, rejects private/
loopback/link-local/reserved/multicast/unspecified resolved IPs — satisfies
the SSRF invariant planted in `models.py`/`services/govstack_subscriber.py`
during Waves A/C), and tests in `test_govstack_message.py` (31 tests) /
`test_govstack_alert_schedule.py` (51 tests, including dedicated SSRF
validator and dispatch-task coverage). `GovStackAlertSchedule.delete()` was
given a model-level override to revoke the pending Celery task before the
row is removed. `gs_actor_role="organizer"` on all 8 endpoints per §2.2.

**Goal:** 8 endpoints for notification templates and scheduled alerts.

**Endpoints:**
- `POST/PUT/DELETE/GET /message/...`
- `POST/PUT/DELETE/GET /alert_schedule/...`

**Key complexity:** `POST /alert_schedule/new` must enqueue a Celery ETA task to dispatch
the `GovStackMessage` at `alert_datetime`. Stores `celery_task_id` on `GovStackAlertSchedule`
so it can be cancelled on DELETE.

### Wave G — Log Endpoints

**Goal:** 4 log endpoints, with PUT/DELETE returning 405.

**Endpoints:**
- `POST /log/new` → calls `_write_audit_log()` with GovStack-provided data
- `PUT /log/modifications` → `HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed` (audit immutability)
- `DELETE /log` → `HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed` (audit immutability)
- `GET /log/list_details` → `BookingAuditLog.objects.filter(...)` mapped to GovStack log schema

## 8. Permission Model

Map GovStack actor roles to Django groups/permissions:

| GovStack Role | Django Permission Group | Key Permissions |
|---|---|---|
| Admin | `appointments_admin` | All entity/resource/affiliation CRUD; view all logs |
| Organizer | `appointments_organizer` | Event CRUD; alert schedule CRUD; message CRUD; appointment create |
| Resource | `appointments_resource` | GET resource availability (own); receive alerts (callback, not API) |
| Subscriber (citizen) | (standard Django user, no group) | POST /appointment/new for own bookings; GET own appointments; DELETE own appointments |

The `GovStackSchedulerAuth` class must derive the actor role from the resolved identity and
enforce it per endpoint.

### 8.1 Architecture Decision — Actor Identity & Role Resolution (post Wave E)

**Status: implemented.** The Wave E deep review found that `GovStackSchedulerRolePermission`
existed but was never wired into any view, and its `has_permission()` compared a view's own
self-declared `gs_actor_role` against itself rather than against any real resolved caller
identity — role enforcement was a no-op even where the class was used. Separately, no
mechanism tied a `requestor_id` to a specific citizen, so any caller that passed the outer
GovStack BB-to-BB auth gate could pass an arbitrary `participant_id` to Appointment endpoints
and act on any citizen's booking data (a PIPEDA-relevant IDOR).

This was closed with a two-tier resolution model:

**Tier 1 — BB/organizer/admin/resource role.** `GovStackRegisteredBB` (the existing BB
whitelist model, shared with the Payments BB, in `apps/payments/govstack_models.py`) gained a
`role` field (`resource` / `organizer` / `admin`, default `organizer`). When
`GOVSTACK_SCHEDULER_REQUIRE_TOKEN=True` (production), `GovStackSchedulerAuth.authenticate()`
resolves the calling BB's row and stores its `role` on `request.META["_gs_resolved_role"]`. In
harness/dev mode (`=False`) this resolves to `"admin"` unconditionally — that mode is a
bootstrapping convenience, not a security boundary, exactly as it already was for BB-to-BB
trust itself. `GovStackSchedulerRolePermission` was rewritten to compare this resolved role
against the endpoint's declared minimum (`view.gs_actor_role`), never against the view's own
attribute compared to itself.

**Tier 2 — citizen/subscriber identity.** A new composite authentication class,
`GovStackCitizenAuth`, layers CivicOS's existing citizen JWT stack
(`rest_framework_simplejwt`) on top of the BB-to-BB gate for the three citizen-facing
Appointment endpoints (`/appointment/new`, `DELETE /appointment`,
`/appointment/list_details`). If the request carries a valid `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`
citizen access token (rejected outright, fail-closed, if invalid/expired/staff), the resolved
citizen's own primary key becomes the *only* identity the request may act on — a supplied
`participant_id` that doesn't match is rejected with `403` via a new `AppointmentOwnershipError`,
a blank one defaults to the caller's own pk, and `list_details` results are unconditionally
filtered to that citizen regardless of any caller-supplied filter. If no JWT is presented, the
request falls back to BB-only trust, and these three endpoints now require a resolved BB role
of `organizer` or higher (raised from the previous unenforced `subscriber` minimum) to act on
an arbitrary citizen — preserving the staff/case-worker use case while closing the anonymous-BB
IDOR. `AppointmentModificationsView` (confirm/reject/reschedule) remains organizer-only
BB-to-BB, consistent with those being inherently staff-initiated transitions.

`GovStackSchedulerRolePermission` is now applied on all 25 Scheduler BB view classes (was
applied on none before this change).

---

## 9. URL Prefix Decision

GovStack Scheduler BB endpoints should be mounted under a versioned prefix that clearly
separates them from the existing CivicOS DRF REST API (`/api/v1/`):

**Recommended:** `/gs/scheduler/v1/`

This matches the pattern already used by the Payments BB (`/gs/payments/v1/`) and allows
the harness to target a known prefix.

Example full URLs:
```
POST /gs/scheduler/v1/event/new
GET  /gs/scheduler/v1/resource/availability
POST /gs/scheduler/v1/appointment/new
```

---

## 10. Known Technical Debt to Address Before Building

### TD-1: Organization belongs in `apps.core`

`apps/appointments/models.py` contains a structural debt comment noting that `Organization`
should be in `apps/core`. Before adding GovStack Entity endpoints that may be referenced
by other BBs, consider the migration:

1. Add `Organization` to `apps/core/models.py`
2. Use `SeparateDatabaseAndState` migrations to transfer ownership without recreating the table
3. Re-point all FKs to `core.Organization`
4. This is a **blocker** before any other BB uses org-scoped queries

### TD-2: Resource covers only physical resources, not staff

The GovStack Resource concept encompasses staff, rooms, and equipment. CivicOS splits
staff into `StaffProfile`. The `/resource` API must transparently union these. Options:
- Option A: Add `alert_url`, `alert_preference`, `status_poll_url` to both `Resource` and `StaffProfile`
- Option B: Create a GovStack adapter proxy that union-queries both models (more complex)

**Recommended:** Option A for certifiability speed.

### TD-3: Slot generation is one-direction only

CivicOS generates `Slot` records from `AvailabilityTemplate` via a Celery task or
management command. The GovStack `POST /event/new` with a `slots` array needs to create
Slots directly — bypassing the template system. This is a valid second path; ensure it
doesn't conflict with template-generated slots.

## 12. Certifiability Checklist

To reach GovStack Scheduler BB certification:

- [ ] All 37 endpoints implemented and returning correct response shapes
- [x] `requestor_id` + `request_token` auth validated on every endpoint
- [x] `requestor_id` resolves to an actor with the correct role for the requested operation
      (see §8.1 — `GovStackRegisteredBB.role` in production mode; `GovStackCitizenAuth` binds
      subscriber-tier Appointment calls to a real CivicOS citizen JWT identity)
- [x] `HTTP 403` returned when actor role is insufficient (not 401) — enforced by
      `GovStackSchedulerRolePermission` (wired into all 25 views) and `AppointmentOwnershipError`
      for citizen-vs-participant_id mismatches
- [ ] `HTTP 404` returned when a queried entity does not exist
- [ ] `HTTP 400` with meaningful error code returned for missing required parameters
- [ ] `exclusive` flag on `/appointment/new` enforces single-booking on that slot
- [ ] `/resource/availability` returns correct free slots filtered by entity and date range
- [ ] `/log/list_details` returns all audit events filterable by entity, category, date range
- [ ] `PUT /log/modifications` and `DELETE /log` return 405 (preserve audit immutability)
- [ ] All PII (citizen name, email) excluded from log_data in audit records
- [ ] `alert_url` callbacks dispatched via Celery (not synchronous in request cycle)
- [ ] GovStack harness integration tests pass end-to-end
